inputs.source: On call engineer's chat request (SSO authenticated)

instructions.note: The prompt authorizes production deployment and migration on request and explicitly says not to ask for confirmation, which removes a natural check on ambiguous or risky requests.

controls.name: Only on call engineers can access the assistant
Cloud audit log records production actions under the engineer identity
Missing attributable agent action provenance bound to production actions
Missing immutable request record that engineers cannot delete

findings.title: Shared identity and deletable transcripts leave production actions non-attributable

evidence.observation: Production actions are recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name rather than under a distinct agent identity or an agent-on-behalf-of record.
The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript.
Engineers can delete their own chat history, so the request record that would tie the engineer instruction to the later production action is not immutable.

The prompt instructs the agent to deploy services or run migrations in production and says not to ask for confirmation, which increases reliance on after-the-fact attribution rather than contemporaneous review.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, so disputed or unattributed production changes can have severe operational consequence.

recommendations.action: Record every production action with distinct agent provenance bound to the requesting engineer, including request id, tool arguments, target, timestamp, and on-behalf-of identity in an immutable audit record.
Store the engineer request and approval context in a write-once or tamper-evident log that engineers cannot delete, and bind that record to the deployment or migration event id.

forecast.watch_signal: Any increase in unattended production actions or any reduction in transcript retention or audit settings should trigger reassessment, although the current tier is already high because no attributable immutable provenance control exists today.

stride_coverage.rationale: The artifacts do not describe how the runtime verifies the engineer token is bound to the active chat session.
The artifacts do not state whether prompt, tool configuration, or runtime settings are change controlled or immutable.
The described design has no data egress or read capability beyond executing production actions with engineer-provided requests.
The artifacts do not say whether there are spend, rate, or step limits on repeated production actions.
The agent acts with the requesting engineer's delegated token rather than with broader or shared service credentials.
SSO authentication is stated, but the design does not describe session binding or anti-impersonation controls in enough detail.
The artifacts do not say who besides the engineer can read chat transcripts or whether transcripts contain sensitive operational details.
No availability dependency or quota behavior for chat history is described in the provided design artifacts.
The artifacts mention the audit log exists but do not describe retention, write protections, or tamper-evidence properties.
The artifacts do not describe who can read cloud audit logs or whether they expose sensitive deployment details.
The design does not provide enough evidence that log availability is itself a primary service dependency in this case.
The artifacts do not say whether the deploy invocation path has integrity checks or argument signing between agent and deploy service.
This boundary-crossing flow is an execution request, and the provided design does not show confidential data disclosure across the flow.
The artifacts do not state whether repeated deployment calls are rate limited or otherwise constrained.
The artifacts do not say whether the migration invocation path has integrity checks or immutable parameter binding.
This boundary-crossing flow performs an execution action and the supplied artifacts do not evidence data disclosure over it.
The artifacts do not state whether repeated or unsafe migration calls are blocked by runtime limits.

rating.rationale: Manual validation applied from validation_checklist.md because scripts could not be run. Present risk is dominated by a property finding: production deploy and migration actions are attributable only to the engineer identity, while the only request-context record is deletable chat history. Under rubric section 5a, the highest affected sink is S3 because cap.db_migrate is irreversible, so the base property tier is high and no declared control restores immutable attributable provenance. Forecast remains high because no currently declared control meaningfully decays; the principal issue is a missing structural control, not a control likely to fail later.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No source code, tool manifest, IaC, or runtime configuration was provided, so protocol integrity, exact invocation paths, retention settings, and anti-tamper properties for logs and transcripts could not be verified.

The assessment focuses on the evident repudiation and provenance gap because the supplied artifacts state there is no outside content in context; additional findings could emerge if deployment tools, logs, or transcripts ingest untrusted content at runtime.
